utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good morning, everybody. Madam Registrar, could you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour. This is case IT-08-91-A, the Prosecutor versus Mico Stanisic and Stojan Zupljanin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Could I have appearances for the parties, please. Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAIG
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour. Laurel Baig for the Prosecution, joined my colleague Katharine Marsden, our Case Manager Colin Nawrot, and interns Marcel Kolesar and Caspar Plomp.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, madam. Appearances for Appellant Stanisic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour. Slobodan Zecevic and Stephane Bourgon appearing for Mr. Stanisic this morning. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. And appearances for Appellant Zupljanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. President. Dragan Krgovic appearing for Zupljanin Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Before I proceed any further, can all parties follow the proceedings in a language that they understand? Mr. Stanisic. THE APPELLANT STANISIC: [Interpretation] Yes, I can. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Zupljanin. THE APPELLANT ZUPLJANIN: [Interpretation] Yes, I can follow. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The same applies to the Defence counsel. All of you? Okay. Now this Status Conference is called in accordance with Rule 65 bis of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence of this Tribunal. Rule 65 bis, paragraph (B), requires a Status Conference to be convened within 120 days after the filing of a Notice of Appeal and, thereafter, within 120 days after the last Status Conference. The purpose is to allow any person in custody pending appeal the opportunity to raise issues in relation thereto, including the mental and physical condition of that person. In the present case, the parties filed their notices of appeal on 13th May 2013, and the first Status Conference was held on 4th September, 2013. The second to seventh Status Conferences were held on 11 December 2013; 9th April, 24th July and 12th November 2014; and 9th March and 30th June 2015 respectively. Today's Status Conference is the eighth in this appeal and was scheduled pursuant to an order issued by myself on the 8th of September, 2015. I will now proceed first to inquire in the status of the detention conditions and health situations of the two appellants, Mr. Stanisic and Mr. Zupljanin. I start with you, Mr. Stanisic. If you have any concerns in relation to the condition of your detention or your state of health, I would invite you to raise them now. And, if you prefer, this discussion with take place in private session. THE APPELLANT STANISIC: [Interpretation] Your Honour, there is nothing to raise. Things are normal for the time being. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. Now I refer to you, Mr. Zupljanin. Same question: If you have any concerns in relation to the condition of your detention or your state of health, I would invite you to raise them now. And, again, if you prefer, this discussion can take place in private session. THE APPELLANT ZUPLJANIN: [Interpretation] As Mr. Stanisic said, the situation is normal. The conditions are the same. It is only time that is passing by, and we are getting older. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So am, I Mr. Zupljanin. Thank you. And so is everybody else. Usually at this point in the proceedings, I would outline the recent procedural history in this case. However, I note that there has been no publicly filed motions or decisions since the last Status Conference of 30th June, and I will therefore now move onto the final part of today's Status Conference, which is any issues that you would like to raise. I'll start with the Prosecution. Ms. Baig, is there any issue the Prosecution would like to raise.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAIG
utterances.text: Your Honour, I only wish to reiterate our request to have as much possible advance notice of the scheduling of the eventual appeals hearing. As we get closer to the judicial recess, the winter judicial recess, it becomes more and more important for us to know whether the hearing is happening before the recess or after the recess so that we can enable our staff to take a holiday, for example. We're all waiting to get more information, and we'd appreciate any guidance that you might be able to give us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Baig. Mr. Zecevic or Mr. Bourgon.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: We join with the Prosecution concerning the date of the oral hearing, oral appeal hearing. And we don't have anything else, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Krgovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, we also join with the Prosecution concerning the date of the oral hearing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Do the appellants, Stanisic and Zupljanin, have you got any issue that you would like to raise? Okay. I saw both indicating that they don't. So let me explain this. When we had the last Status Conference, and I checked to make sure that I will be as precise as possible, I remember that the Prosecution, in particular, but also the Defence, raised the same concerns, and you had at the time renewed your requests to have at least eight weeks' notice of the appeal hearing. Now, during that same Status Conference, I had informed you that the plan was to have the appeal hearing this year. At the time, we were aiming for November. The idea being to then deliver the Judgement next year in June. Let me put it like this: The end date for the appeal, June of 2016, remains, and our plan is firmly to deliver the Judgement during that month. However, as of today, I am not in a position to confirm for sure if the hearing will take place in December - certainly not November - in December or early in January. It's not because we have fallen behind in our work. It's a combination of reasons. One reason is that I am obsessed with making sure that the prep doc that will be circulated to my colleagues is of the highest quality possible, and it would enable them to follow the submissions that we will receive during the hearing. So that is a laborious exercise, and it may take a little bit more time. However, the real problem is that due to the changes in the composition of the Benches in Butare and Stanisic and Simatovic and in my case, the Stanisic and Zupljanin case, we have ended up with four Judges being on all these three Benches. Now, there are priorities in life, as you know, and we have to be careful to respect those priorities, and two priorities which are very important - believe me - is that both Butare and Stanisic and Simatovic have to be concluded before the end of this year, have to be concluded before the end of this year for a very simple reason. Butare is an ICTR appeal, and after December 31st, the ICTR will no longer exist, so it has to be -- the Judgement has to be delivered before the demise of the ICTR. And in Stanisic and Simatovic, one the Judges, if not two, I think one is an ICTR Judge, and since there cannot be any ICTR Judges beyond the 31st of December of this year, that case also has to finish before that date. That creates problems in the sense that the same Judges have to look into draft Judgement running into several hundreds of pages in one case, another draft Judgement of considerable importance and length in another case, plus deal with the prep doc that I will be circulating. And the prep doc in this case, in Stanisic and Zupljanin, will certainly be circulated pretty soon, I can tell you, pretty soon, because we are almost ready. But whether I will be in a position to summon the hearing or to fix the hearing in December, I am beginning to have doubts. I'm making an effort. It depends on the date when we deliver the Judgement in Butare. Because basically that - economising the utmost on time - basically means four days. To go there and to prepare, have the delivery of Judgement, and fly back it takes you four days, and those are four days which are taken from a crucial week when I can't do much more. And it coincides also with the beginning -- or with the end of the session. That is the last week that we are working before we go on holiday. So the problem of needing to know when is not only your problem, it's also my problem. I also have staff that need to go on holiday. I also have colleagues that have a right for their recess break, so please understand and believe me that I'm doing my absolute best. Now you requested eight weeks. If I can manage to fit the hearing in December, I'm still in time to give you eight weeks pre-advance notice. If we're talking of January, I have to take into account the end of the recess. I can't expect anyone to come here before the end of the recess. And probably if we're speaking of January, it will be the -- the earliest will be probably the 15th or something like that. However, that would mean that you would -- if I were to give you that advance notice now, you would have three months. So what I can tell you is I am in discussions with some of my colleagues who are involved in the other cases and need to know for them to be able to prepare, and once we come to an agreement, which should happen either this week or latest next week, I will be in a position to give you a definitive answer with a definitive approximate date. All right? Thank you. Is there anything else you would like to raise? No. So that's all for today. I close this Status Conference and I thank you all for attending.
